---
title: "Why leaves crinkle: differential growth in a disc"
format: html
image: 'leaf_preview.png'
categories: [Differential equations, Geometry, Calculus]
---

Why are some leaves more wrinkled than others? And what causes this to happen?

Consider a circular disc 
of radius, $R$.

The perimeter  is $2\pi R$ whilst the area of the circle is $\pi R^2$.
It can be shown that this circle is the most efficient way to contain the area $\pi R^2$.

Now imagine distorting the disc so that the circumference is wrinkled. The cirumference of the wrinkled shape is larger than $2 \pi R$. 

In the plant at this stop, notice that the leaves are wrinkled rather than smooth. Why does evolution find this shape for this particular plant and how does it happen?
![](bg_wrinkle_crop.png)


One way to make a wrinkled surface is to have different regions of the surface grow at different rates. Essentially, take a circle  and allow the outer region  to grow at a faster rate than the inner region. The effect of the differential growth is that the faster growing region wrinkles. 

::: {#fig-leaf-growth}

```{=html}
<div id="leaf-app" style="display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:24px; align-items:flex-start; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; max-width:960px;">
  <div style="flex: 0 0 260px; min-width:220px;">
    <h5 style="margin:0 0 8px 0;">Growth</h5>
    <label for="leaf-krim" style="display:block; font-size:14px; margin-bottom:4px;">Rim growth rate, relative to the centre: <strong id="leaf-krim-val">1.6</strong></label>
    <input id="leaf-krim" type="range" min="1.0" max="3.0" step="0.1" value="1.6" style="width:100%;">
    <label for="leaf-m" style="display:block; font-size:14px; margin:14px 0 4px 0;">Number of ripples around the rim: <strong id="leaf-m-val">7</strong></label>
    <input id="leaf-m" type="range" min="3" max="16" step="1" value="7" style="width:100%;">
    <hr style="margin:16px 0; border:none; border-top:1px solid #ddd;">
    <div id="leaf-summary" style="font-size:14px; line-height:1.6;"></div>
  </div>
  <div style="flex: 1 1 420px; min-width:320px;">
    <canvas id="leaf-surface" width="640" height="480" style="width:100%; max-width:640px; height:auto; display:block;"></canvas>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Differential growth in a disc -- the maths (ported 1:1 from the
  // original Python/Shinylive version, no numerical shortcuts taken).
  // Runs as plain JavaScript, entirely in the browser -- no Python
  // runtime to download, unlike the Shinylive apps elsewhere on this
  // site.
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  var R = 1.0;
  var PROFILE_EXPONENT = 3.0;
  var N_RADIAL = 36;
  var N_AZIMUTHAL = 96;
  var N_QUAD = 120;

  function growthProfile(rho, kRim) {
    return 1.0 + (kRim - 1.0) * Math.pow(rho / R, PROFILE_EXPONENT);
  }

  function loopArclength(rho, amplitude, m) {
    var dphi = (2 * Math.PI) / N_QUAD;
    var sum = 0.0;
    for (var i = 0; i < N_QUAD; i++) {
      var phi = i * dphi;
      var term = amplitude * m * Math.cos(m * phi);
      sum += Math.sqrt(rho * rho + term * term);
    }
    return sum * dphi;
  }

  function solveAmplitude(rho, gamma, m) {
    if (rho < 1e-9 || gamma <= 1.0 + 1e-9) return 0.0;
    var target = 2 * Math.PI * rho * gamma;
    var lo = 0.0, hi = rho;
    var tries = 0;
    while (loopArclength(rho, hi, m) < target && tries < 40) {
      hi *= 1.7;
      tries++;
    }
    for (var iter = 0; iter < 60; iter++) {
      var mid = 0.5 * (lo + hi);
      if (loopArclength(rho, mid, m) < target) {
        lo = mid;
      } else {
        hi = mid;
      }
      if (hi - lo < 1e-7 * rho) break;
    }
    return 0.5 * (lo + hi);
  }

  function buildSurface(kRim, m) {
    var rhoVals = new Float64Array(N_RADIAL);
    var gammaVals = new Float64Array(N_RADIAL);
    var ampVals = new Float64Array(N_RADIAL);
    for (var i = 0; i < N_RADIAL; i++) {
      var rho = (R * i) / (N_RADIAL - 1);
      rhoVals[i] = rho;
      var gamma = growthProfile(rho, kRim);
      gammaVals[i] = gamma;
      ampVals[i] = solveAmplitude(rho, gamma, m);
    }
    return { rho: rhoVals, gamma: gammaVals, amp: ampVals };
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Colour: a small hand-picked approximation of matplotlib's YlGn
  // sequential colormap, interpolated linearly between stops.
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  var YLGN_STOPS = [
    [255, 255, 229], [247, 252, 185], [217, 240, 163],
    [173, 221, 142], [120, 198, 121], [65, 171, 93],
    [35, 132, 67], [0, 104, 55], [0, 69, 41]
  ];
  function ylgn(t) {
    t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));
    var n = YLGN_STOPS.length - 1;
    var idx = t * n;
    var i0 = Math.floor(idx);
    var i1 = Math.min(i0 + 1, n);
    var f = idx - i0;
    var c0 = YLGN_STOPS[i0], c1 = YLGN_STOPS[i1];
    var r = Math.round(c0[0] + (c1[0] - c0[0]) * f);
    var g = Math.round(c0[1] + (c1[1] - c0[1]) * f);
    var b = Math.round(c0[2] + (c1[2] - c0[2]) * f);
    return "rgb(" + r + "," + g + "," + b + ")";
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  // A small orthographic elevation/azimuth camera, replacing matplotlib's
  // Axes3D -- projects (x,y,z) world points to 2D screen coordinates and
  // gives each a depth value for painter's-algorithm back-to-front sort.
  // -------------------------------------------------------------------
  function makeCamera(elevationDeg, azimuthDeg) {
    var el = (elevationDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
    var az = (azimuthDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
    var forward = [
      Math.cos(el) * Math.cos(az),
      Math.cos(el) * Math.sin(az),
      Math.sin(el)
    ];
    var worldUp = [0, 0, 1];
    var right = normalize(cross(forward, worldUp));
    var camUp = cross(right, forward);
    return {
      project: function (p) {
        return {
          x: dot(p, right),
          y: dot(p, camUp),
          depth: dot(p, forward)
        };
      }
    };
  }
  function cross(a, b) {
    return [a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1], a[2] * b[0] - a[0] * b[2], a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]];
  }
  function dot(a, b) { return a[0] * b[0] + a[1] * b[1] + a[2] * b[2]; }
  function normalize(v) {
    var len = Math.sqrt(dot(v, v));
    return [v[0] / len, v[1] / len, v[2] / len];
  }

  var camera = makeCamera(38, -60);

  function worldPoint(rho, phi, amp, m) {
    return [rho * Math.cos(phi), rho * Math.sin(phi), amp * Math.sin(m * phi)];
  }

  function drawSurface(canvas, surf, kRim, m) {
    var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d");
    var W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);

    var rhoVals = surf.rho, ampVals = surf.amp;
    var zSpan = 0.05;
    for (var i = 0; i < ampVals.length; i++) zSpan = Math.max(zSpan, Math.abs(ampVals[i]));

    var nPhi = N_AZIMUTHAL;
    var quads = [];
    for (var ri = 0; ri < N_RADIAL - 1; ri++) {
      var rho0 = rhoVals[ri], rho1 = rhoVals[ri + 1];
      var a0 = ampVals[ri], a1 = ampVals[ri + 1];
      for (var pj = 0; pj < nPhi; pj++) {
        var phi0 = (2 * Math.PI * pj) / nPhi;
        var phi1 = (2 * Math.PI * (pj + 1)) / nPhi;

        var corners = [
          worldPoint(rho0, phi0, a0, m),
          worldPoint(rho1, phi0, a1, m),
          worldPoint(rho1, phi1, a1, m),
          worldPoint(rho0, phi1, a0, m)
        ];
        var proj = corners.map(camera.project);
        var depth = (proj[0].depth + proj[1].depth + proj[2].depth + proj[3].depth) / 4;
        var zAvg = (corners[0][2] + corners[1][2] + corners[2][2] + corners[3][2]) / 4;
        quads.push({ proj: proj, depth: depth, colour: ylgn((zAvg + zSpan) / (2 * zSpan)) });
      }
    }
    quads.sort(function (a, b) { return a.depth - b.depth; });

    var minX = Infinity, maxX = -Infinity, minY = Infinity, maxY = -Infinity;
    quads.forEach(function (q) {
      q.proj.forEach(function (p) {
        minX = Math.min(minX, p.x); maxX = Math.max(maxX, p.x);
        minY = Math.min(minY, p.y); maxY = Math.max(maxY, p.y);
      });
    });
    var pad = 0.08 * Math.max(maxX - minX, maxY - minY, 1e-6);
    var scaleX = (W - 40) / (maxX - minX + 2 * pad);
    var scaleY = (H - 60) / (maxY - minY + 2 * pad);
    var scale = Math.min(scaleX, scaleY);
    var cx = W / 2 - scale * (minX + maxX) / 2;
    var cy = H / 2 + scale * (minY + maxY) / 2;

    function toScreen(p) {
      return [cx + scale * p.x, cy - scale * p.y];
    }

    quads.forEach(function (q) {
      var pts = q.proj.map(toScreen);
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(pts[0][0], pts[0][1]);
      for (var k = 1; k < pts.length; k++) ctx.lineTo(pts[k][0], pts[k][1]);
      ctx.closePath();
      ctx.fillStyle = q.colour;
      ctx.fill();
    });

    ctx.fillStyle = "#333";
    ctx.font = "13px -apple-system, sans-serif";
    ctx.textAlign = "center";
    var title;
    if (kRim <= 1.02) title = "uniform growth — stays flat";
    else if (zSpan < 0.08) title = "mild rim growth — gentle waviness";
    else title = "rim growing much faster than centre — strong crinkling";
    ctx.fillText(title, W / 2, 20);
  }

  var krimSlider = document.getElementById("leaf-krim");
  var mSlider = document.getElementById("leaf-m");
  var krimVal = document.getElementById("leaf-krim-val");
  var mVal = document.getElementById("leaf-m-val");
  var surfaceCanvas = document.getElementById("leaf-surface");
  var summaryDiv = document.getElementById("leaf-summary");

  function render() {
    var kRim = parseFloat(krimSlider.value);
    var m = parseInt(mSlider.value, 10);
    krimVal.textContent = kRim.toFixed(1);
    mVal.textContent = String(m);

    var surf = buildSurface(kRim, m);
    drawSurface(surfaceCanvas, surf, kRim, m);

    var excessPct = (kRim - 1.0) * 100.0;
    var maxAmp = surf.amp[surf.amp.length - 1];
    var html = "<strong>Excess rim growth:</strong> " + excessPct.toFixed(0) + "% faster than the centre<br><br>" +
      "<strong>Max ripple height (relative to the disc radius):</strong> " + maxAmp.toFixed(2) + "<br><br>";
    if (kRim <= 1.02) {
      html += "Every part of the disc is growing at the same rate, so there's no extra length to fit in anywhere — the disc just scales up uniformly and <strong>stays flat</strong>.";
    } else if (maxAmp < 0.08) {
      html += "The rim only needs a little extra length, which fits with a gentle, barely-visible waviness.";
    } else {
      html += "The rim needs much more circumferential length than a flat disc of that radius can provide — the only way to fit it in is to <strong>ripple out of the plane</strong>, the same mechanism behind real crinkled leaf margins, lettuce, and torn plastic sheets.";
    }
    summaryDiv.innerHTML = html;
  }

  krimSlider.addEventListener("input", render);
  mSlider.addEventListener("input", render);
  render();
})();
</script>
```


A differential-growth leaf simulator: drag the rim growth rate up from 1.0 and a flat disc is forced to crinkle, exactly as a real leaf margin does when it grows faster than the tissue near its centre.
:::


<!--
A flat, round piece of paper can only stretch into another flat shape -- to make it curve into a dome or ripple into a wave, you have to cut it, fold it, or force extra material in somewhere. Leaves, lettuce, and the frilly edge of a torn plastic bag all do exactly this without any cutting, just by growing unevenly.

Model a leaf as a disc that starts perfectly flat. Every small ring of tissue at distance $\rho$ from the centre grows by some local factor $\gamma(\rho) \ge 1$. If $\gamma$ is the same everywhere, every ring simply gets longer by the same proportion, and the disc scales up while staying completely flat -- a bigger, flat leaf.

But real leaf margins often grow *faster* than the tissue near the midrib. Suppose $\gamma(\rho)$ increases towards the rim. Then the ring at the rim needs more circumference than a flat disc of that same radius can supply -- there simply isn't room for the extra length in a flat plane. The ring has nowhere to put the surplus except out of the page: it ripples up and down around its circumference, trading flatness for the extra length it's been given. The more excess growth there is, the taller the ripples have to be.

This is a real, well-studied piece of mathematics -- non-uniform growth prescribes a *target metric* with nonzero Gaussian curvature, and Gauss's own *Theorema Egregium* says a surface's Gaussian curvature can't change under bending alone, only under stretching. A flat disc has zero curvature everywhere; a disc that's been told to grow unevenly is being asked to have nonzero curvature; the only way to reconcile the two is to leave the plane. The mechanism was worked out in detail for real torn plastic sheets and leaves by Sharon, Marder & Swinney (*"Leaves, flowers and garbage bags: Making waves"*, 2004) and given a rigorous elastic-sheet treatment by Klein, Efrati & Sharon (*"Shaping of Elastic Sheets by Prescription of Non-Euclidean Metrics"*, 2007).

The simulation below is a deliberately simplified, honest proxy for that mechanism, not a solved elasticity problem. Each ring is kept at its flat projected radius and independently ripples as a simple sine wave, $z(\rho, \phi) = A(\rho)\sin(m\phi)$, just enough to supply exactly the extra length its own growth rate demands -- found numerically, by searching for the amplitude whose true (curved) arc-length matches the target grown length. A real leaf would also let neighbouring rings share the load elastically, and wouldn't necessarily settle into one clean ripple count, but the qualitative story is the same one real growing tissue produces: **uniform growth stays flat, and growth concentrated at the rim forces the sheet to crinkle** -- and the more excess growth, the more pronounced the crinkling.

Drag **rim growth rate** from 1 (flat) upward and watch the disc lift into a ripple. The **number of ripples** slider changes how many waves share the excess length around the rim, without changing how much total extra length there is.


-->
